title: 3 steps to follow for Bigger Arms
summary: NH lays out three stages for arm growth: compounds that involve the arms, then isolation added on top (starting at about 3 sets a week and increasing frequency, using supersets), then a dedicated arm day for late-intermediate and advanced lifters who have stalled. He warns against constantly rotating curl variations and says programming matters more than exercise choice.
claims: For naturals, programming drives muscle building; exercise selection is a by-product
Using a huge number of curl variations reduces neurological and technical adaptation, so you keep relearning instead of growing
For novices anything grows the arms, even curling a chair, so a strategy working for a novice does not make it good
Step one: compound movements that involve the arms, such as chin-ups and rows for the biceps and horizontal and vertical presses for the triceps
NH recommends novices start isolation right away, even just 3 sets of curls a week, to get used to the movement
Only rare outliers grow their arms on compounds alone, and usually only the biceps or triceps, never both
Step two: add isolation on top of the compounds, not instead of them; this stage can last a very long time
Forearms follow the same steps: deadlifts and pull-ups first, then isolation
Presses barely hit the long head of the triceps, so overhead triceps extensions with shoulder flexion are crucial for full arm development
Start isolation once a week, then go to twice and three times a week; small muscles trained in a safe range recover fast even though their work capacity is low
For arms, intensity is fixed at failure and per-session volume is limited, so growth comes from raising frequency and weekly volume over time
Do isolation as straight sets with 2 minutes rest only while learning it; graduate quickly to supersets with compounds, such as curls with bench accessories or skull crushers after pull-ups
Step three: an arm day where curls and triceps extensions come first when you are freshest, though it should still include some compounds
Arm days built only from cable isolation are not how you grow
An arm day costs a full training slot; for powerlifters it is idiotic, for bodybuilders it makes sense
On an arm day, superset everything and use giant sets
Stage two eventually runs out of room for progression because adding sets stops being realistic; the arm day gives space for a main curl plus secondary curls
Novices belong in step one, late novices and intermediates in step two, and late-intermediate to advanced lifters in step three; a novice arm day is a waste
Stalled arm growth when advanced does not mean you hit your natural limit; it means it is time for an arm day
Arm development matters greatly for aesthetics because the limbs extend across the physique, as do the legs
exercises: compounds for triceps; barely hit triceps long head
start ~3 sets/wk; superset with presses or pulls
targets triceps long head for the full arm look
